text: Owner's decision (2026-11-24) on the expiry failure boundary: a completed till sale or return is ALWAYS posted centrally; the expiry module may never leave it parked as REJECTED for manual replay. Required behaviour for in/expiry-sale-transactions: (1) every expiry-side AppError during central acceptance (missing markdown/item/balance before the current catch, replay/bounds mismatch, payroll persistence rejection raised as AppError, anything else the expiry or payroll-source port throws as AppError) becomes a durable unallocated exception with its diagnostic, exactly like the stale-approval and budget cases: the sale posts, stock and money post, no employee charge is made. (2) The expiry part must not be able to roll back the sale's own stock and money posting: decide and document how (savepoint around the expiry port call inside the same transaction, so a failed expiry step rolls back only itself) and prove that a failed payroll insert leaves no half liability. (3) Technical faults (non-AppError: programming errors, DB timeouts, lock timeouts) keep today's behaviour: central transaction rolled back, edge event PENDING with retry, no duplicates on recovery; add the lock-timeout 55P03 case you named as untested. (4) An admin screen or report must show the unallocated exceptions so that the owner can see and settle them; say where. (5) Tests: your fault-injection suite extended so that each AppError class ends in ACCEPTED + unallocated exception + correct stock and money, and none ends in pos_sync_rejections. Write this policy into ADR-0245. HR and salary branches are not affected and may proceed.
